findings.message: Validate the manifest name before constructing the output directory. A remote manifest can supply a name such as `../../some-directory`, since `validateSkillset` only checks that it is a string. Joining that name here moves the output directory outside the temporary staging area, and `safePath` then treats that escaped directory as trusted. Reject path components in names or use a generated temporary directory so installing an untrusted skillset cannot overwrite files elsewhere.

Check directory boundaries rather than string prefixes. For a base directory `/tmp/spm/foo`, a manifest file path resolving to `/tmp/spm/foo-other/file` passes this check despite escaping the staging directory. Traversal segments are still accepted in manifest file lists and relative sources. Check containment using a path-relative comparison or a prefix including the directory separator.

Preserve the ref specified in a GitHub URL. Installing a URL containing `tree/develop/...` discards `develop`, after which `resolveIdentifier` always selects the repository's default branch. This either downloads a different skillset version or fails when the requested path exists only on the specified branch. Carry the URL ref through parsing and use default-branch discovery only when no ref was supplied.

Resolve refs independently for cross-repository sources. When a skillset references `@other/repo/path`, this passes the parent repository's ref to the other repository. If the parent defaults to `main` but the referenced repository defaults to `master`, every referenced file returns 404; if both branches exist, the wrong version may be downloaded. Resolve the target repository's default branch for cross-repository entries instead of reusing `location.ref`.
